content: 1. In November 2014, the World Health Organization (WHO) introduced its reproductive health guidelines and tools, providing principles and processes for their adaptation and implementation into national programs. This document was accessed on May 25, 2016. 2. The WHO, in collaboration with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS), the Global Network of Sex Work Projects, the World Bank, and the United Nations Development Programme, developed a comprehensive guide for implementing HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) programs with sex workers. This guide emphasizes practical approaches derived from collaborative interventions and was accessed on May 25, 2016. 3. WHO published consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations. These guidelines were accessed on May 25, 2016. 4. The UNFPA, the Global Forum on MSM (men who have sex with men) & HIV, the United Nations Development Programme, WHO, the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), and the World Bank collaborated to create a guide for implementing comprehensive HIV and STI programs with MSM. This guide provides practical guidance for collaborative interventions and was accessed on May 25, 2016. 5. WHO released consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection. These guidelines provide recommendations for a public health approach and were accessed on May 25, 2016. 6. The UNAIDS/WHO Working Group on Global HIV/AIDS and STI Surveillance published strategies and laboratory methods to strengthen the surveillance of sexually transmitted infections in 2012. 7. WHO regional STI focal points include experts from various regions: Massimo Ghidinelli (Region of the Americas), Lali Khotenashvili (European Region), Ying-Ru Lo (Western Pacific Region), Frank Lule (African Region), Razia Pendse and Ornella Lincetto (South-East Asia Region), and Hamida Khattabi and Gabriela Reidner (Eastern Mediterranean Region). 8. WHO headquarters and departments involved in reproductive health and research include key personnel such as Moazzam Ali, Avni Amin, Rachel Baggaley, Venkatraman Chandra-Mouli, Jane Ferguson, Mario Festin, Mary Lyn Gaffield, Antonio Gerbase, Sami Gottlieb, Silvo Paolo Mariotti, Frances McConville, Lori Newman, Annette Mwansa Nkowane, Anita Sands, Igor Toskin, Marco Vitoria, Ian Askew, Nathalie Broutet, James Kiarie, Lee Sharkey, and Teodora Elvira Wi. 9. The WHO STI Steering Committee and guideline development teams include experts such as Nancy Santesso (methodologist) and systematic review team members from McMaster University, including Housne Begum, Janna-Lina Kerth, Gian Paolo Morgano, Kristie Poole, Nicole Schwab, Matthew Ventresca, Yuan Zhang, and Andrew Zikic. 10. The WHO guidelines for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae were developed with contributions from experts such as Yaw Adu-Sarkodie, Andrew Amato, Gail Bolan, John Changalucha, Francisco Garcia, Sarah Hawkes, King Holmes, David Lewis, Richard Steen, Magnus Unemo, Judith Wasserheit, Thomas Wong, and Kimberly A. Workowski. 11. The WHO reviewed key international guidelines on sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in December 2013 to determine which recommendations required updates. These included guidelines from the CDC (2010), the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV (2006–2011), the Public Health Agency of Canada (2013–2014), the International Union of Sexually Transmitted Infections (IUSTI), the Sexual Health Society of Victoria (2008), and the National Department of Health in South Africa (2009), among others. 12. Based on this review, four categories of STI conditions were prioritized for inclusion in the updated WHO STI guidelines. These included conditions from the 2003 WHO STI guidelines selected for review and update by the Guideline Development Group (GDG).
